links.title: Write Path
links.tooltip: Life of a WRITE, stage by stage

panels.title: Stage 0 — Client (KSC): resolve → connect → read → reconstruct
Not yet instrumented: KSC client read metrics
panels.description: Placeholder for the client stage of the read story. The KSC stats root is not exported yet (gap C1), so Stage 0 is dark in Grafana.

options.content:
**Pending exporter work (gap C1):** the entire KSC client stats root is unexported — no `keinfs_ksc_*` families exist on the exporter. Once C1 lands, this row gains:

- **`kms_resolve`** — read-resolve RTT to KMS (ResolveObjectRead / ResolveObjectHead). Zero on a client-side cache hit.
- **`target_connect`** — HTTP/2 session establishment to KST.
- **`target_read`** — per-fragment read time (per-fragment *sum*: inflates with fan-out and retries; multi-stripe summation caveat applies).
- **`ec_reconstruct`** — genuine Reed–Solomon reconstruction on reads. **This is the ONLY degraded-read signal anywhere in the system**: no KMS or KST metric distinguishes a fast-path read from a degraded read. Until C1 lands, degraded reads are invisible in Grafana. (Note: on *write* flows the same field is a stash hack holding the BeginObject RTT — the exporter must apply the B4 renames before these series appear, or this panel would lie.)
- **`target_payload_validate` / `target_protocol_decode`** — client-side KP2 decode + CRC validation cost.

Until then: infer client health indirectly from Stage 1 resolve latency and Stage 2–4 KST-side read latency.

panels.title: Stage 1 — KMS resolve (ResolveObjectRead, read cache, route cache)
ResolveObjectRead rate & errors
panels.description: Read-resolve RPC rate per KMS instance, plus its error rate. This is the metadata lookup every uncached client read performs. Errors should be 0; a rate collapse while clients are active = clients are being served from their own cache, or resolve is failing upstream.

panels.title: ResolveObjectRead latency (avg / p99 / max)
panels.description: Read-resolve latency per KMS instance. p99 is a pow2-bucketed approximation (quantile-labeled gauge, power-of-2 buckets — steps like 65536 µs are quantization, not workload); avg and max are exact. Healthy resolve on a warm read cache is sub-millisecond; a jump here delays every uncached read before a single data byte moves.

panels.title: ResolveObjectHead rate & latency — populates after next KMS deploy
panels.description: The decentralized head-only resolve (rpc=resolve_object_head). The RPC kind was just added in code (gap C5) — this panel populates after the next KMS deploy; until then it renders no data by design (visible gap, not a broken query). Once live, this is THE decentralized-read metadata-load signal. Latency p99 is pow2-bucketed approx.

panels.title: Read-cache activity (hit / miss / store per second)
panels.description: KMS read-cache phase occurrence rates under rpc=resolve_object_read (derived from phase sample counters). Hits should dominate under a steady read workload; a miss+store surge = cold cache or an invalidation storm (see the invalidations panel). This IS the resolve fast path — misses pay the full store lookup.

panels.title: Read-cache hit %
panels.description: Share of resolve_object_read requests served from the KMS read cache over the current rate window. High (>90%) under steady reads = fast path healthy. A sustained drop means resolves are paying store-lookup cost — correlate with the invalidations panel.

panels.title: Read-cache invalidations (all / namespace / object)
panels.description: Read-cache invalidation rates by scope. Object-scope invalidations track overwrite/delete churn on read-hot keys; namespace- or all-scope spikes wipe large cache regions and will show up as a miss surge + resolve latency bump on the panels to the left. Frequent 'all' invalidations under normal operation are a bug signal.

panels.title: Route cache (hits / misses / discovery)
panels.description: KMS route-cache behavior: how often the shard/route for a key is answered from cache vs requiring a discovery lookup or discovery RPC. Discovery RPCs should be rare after warm-up; a sustained discovery-RPC rate = topology churn or a cache-sizing problem, and it adds RTTs in front of every affected resolve.

panels.title: Queue wait p99: direct-read pool vs packed-serial ingress (µs)
panels.description: execution_queue_wait = wait for the direct-read execution pool (single-chunk direct reads); ingress_queue_wait = wait in the serial ingress lane (packed multi-chunk reads). p99 per target, pow2-bucketed approx. If ingress_queue_wait climbs while execution_queue_wait stays flat, the packed-serial lane is the bottleneck (packed reads queue behind each other); the reverse means the direct-read pool is undersized or the drive is slow. Compare against Stage 3 media phases to separate queueing from media time.

panels.title: kix_lookup p99 per target (µs)
panels.description: Time the read spends resolving chunk locations in the KIX in-memory live map before touching media. p99, pow2-bucketed approx. Normally near-zero (in-memory); growth here points at KIX shard contention or lookup-queue depth — cross-check the KIX dashboards (per-drive detail pending gap C8).

panels.title: Read stream admission rejections (/s)
panels.description: Rate of read streams rejected at admission per target. Must be 0 in a healthy fleet — any non-zero value means clients are being pushed back before execution (admission limits hit) and read latency at the client will spike with retries. Correlate with the queue-wait panel: rejections with high ingress wait = the target is genuinely saturated.

panels.title: Stage 3 — Media read (raw device, direct I/O)
Media read phases p99 per target (µs)
panels.description: The on-drive read decomposition: media_header_validate (chunk header check), media_payload_read (the actual device read — normally dominant), media_payload_copy (buffer copy), media_crc (integrity check). p99, pow2-bucketed approx. If media_payload_read on one target diverges from the fleet, that drive is the laggard; if media_crc grows, suspect CPU contention on the target, not the drive.

panels.title: Media read phase budget — fleet max of last p99 (µs)
panels.description: Worst-target snapshot of each media read phase's current p99 (pow2-bucketed approx). Reads left-to-right as the media time budget: the tallest bar is where the slowest drive spends its read time. Use it to decide which phase to chase in the timeseries panel.

panels.title: Publication retry rate (stale-lane retry, /s)
panels.description: Rate of reads that had to retry because the slot-publication lane served a stale location. This is the degraded-lane early-warning signal on the KST side: a rising retry rate means the slot publication lanes are lagging media commits, and read latency tails will follow. Healthy steady state is ~0.

panels.title: Response phases p99 (rpc=read, µs)
panels.description: Cost of shipping the read result back over KP2/HTTP-2: response_encode, response_send_headers, response_send_body, response_send. p99 per phase across targets, pow2-bucketed approx. Growth in response_send_body with flat media phases = network/flow-control backpressure from the client, not a storage problem.

panels.title: Packed vs total read requests (/s)
panels.description: keinfs_kst_kp2_packed_read_requests rate vs the total read RPC rate per target. The gap between the two is the direct single-chunk read rate. A packed share near 100% under small-object workloads is expected; packed reads take the serial ingress lane (see Stage 2 queue-wait split), so a high packed share plus rising ingress_queue_wait = packing is the throughput limiter.

panels.title: Read payload served per target (B/s)
panels.description: Wire-level read payload bytes/s served from media per target. Note this is fragment/wire bytes, not client logical bytes — with EC striping and packing, wire bytes can exceed logical bytes by a large factor (the 64x sequential read-amplification class of problem). The logical-bytes counterpart is pending gap C3 (see placeholder below).

panels.title: Not yet instrumented: packed-read chunks & logical bytes (read-amplification)
panels.description: Placeholder for the packed-read efficiency metrics that keinexport does not export yet (gap C3).

options.content:
**Pending exporter work (gap C3):** the KST `kp2` stat subtree records `packed_read_chunks` and `packed_read_logical_payload_bytes` (and the write-side equivalents), but keinexport only exports `packed_read_requests`. Once C3 lands, this row gains:

- **Chunks per packed read** (`packed_read_chunks / packed_read_requests`) — packing efficiency; low values mean the packed lane's serialization cost is not being amortized.
- **Logical vs wire bytes** (`packed_read_logical_payload_bytes` vs `keinfs_kst_read_payload_bytes`) — the direct read-amplification ratio. This is the panel that would have caught the 64x sequential-read amplification found in the KFC v2 work.

Until then, read amplification can only be inferred by comparing client-observed goodput against the per-target wire B/s panel above.
